opening_question_spark: Why can a naked statue feel proper when a naked person feels exposed?
entry_transition: Because shame often follows learned rules about where nakedness belongs.
cta: Notice the rule before blaming the body.
body: Families, religions, laws, and customs teach those rules.
They vary across cultures, places, and history.
Chosen privacy feels different from unexpected exposure.
Context can also make nudity feel sexual.
Anticipated staring or judgment can trigger shame.
Art galleries or some beaches may treat nakedness as ordinary.
A changing booth usually expects concealment from strangers.
optional_closing: The skin stayed ordinary; the social meaning changed.
